text: A website for CityCare Hospital in Bengaluru: patients book visits, emergency info

@CEO Three charter gaps in the brief need your call before work starts. The department's recommendation is A on each, because the site is one static file with no backend and the audience is patients, some in distress.
1. Booking scope: (A) a 'Request a visit' form (name, phone, department, preferred date/time) that shows a confirmation and states the hospital will call to confirm; cost: no live slots, low build effort, no false promise of a held appointment. (B) a slot picker showing availability; cost: needs a backend and hospital scheduling data we do not have, so it would be fake and could mislead patients. Recommend A. Choose A or B?
2. Emergency facts: we do not have CityCare's real phone numbers, address or ER hours, and a wrong number on an emergency page is a safety risk. (A) Show clearly marked placeholders for hospital-specific details plus India's public emergency numbers (112 general, 108 ambulance; unverified by us, Audit to check), and make Requester-confirmed real details a done-when item before launch. (B) Invent plausible details for a finished-looking demo; risk: patients could act on false data. Recommend A. Choose A or B?
3. Patient data: the form touches health-related information, which falls under India's DPDP Act 2023. (A) Collect the minimum only (name, phone, department, date), no symptoms or medical history, nothing stored or sent from the page, with a short privacy notice. (B) Also collect symptoms and history; cost: needs secure storage and consent handling we cannot provide in one file. Recommend A. Choose A or B?

@Identity All three: A. The brief is silent on each, so I picked the simplest safe option for a one-file static site.
1. 1. A: 'Request a visit' form with a confirmation that says the hospital will call to confirm. A slot picker would show fake availability and mislead patients.
2. 2. A: clearly marked placeholders for CityCare-specific details, plus 112 (general) and 108 (ambulance) with Audit verifying them. Requester-confirmed real phone, address and ER hours become a done-when item before launch. Invented emergency details are a safety risk.
3. 3. A: collect only name, phone, department and preferred date/time. No symptoms or history, nothing stored or sent from the page, with a short privacy notice. Trade-off: the form is a demo that needs a real backend and consent handling before it takes live requests.

@Adaptation Charter is recorded from the brief and the CEO's three decisions. Propose the workflows that close the done-when list; the form is a demo until a backend and consent handling exist, and the Requester must supply the real hospital details before launch.
@Adaptation Charter valid: statement present, 7 checkable done-when items. Work can start.

@Priority Proposing one build workflow: the whole single-file site (emergency section with 112 and 108, 'Request a visit' form, privacy notice, demo banner, marked placeholders). It closes 5 of the 7 done-when items, and the last two (Requester-confirmed details, Audit sign-off) follow after it. Ask: 8 of the 40 budget, leaving room for one Audit rework cycle and a later swap-in of confirmed details.

proposal.name: Build CityCare single-file site v1
proposal.goal_gap: No site exists (site_versions = 0), so no done-when item is met yet.
proposal.expected_outcome: One index.html (HTML, CSS, JS inline, no build step) with: a top emergency section showing 112 (general) and 108 (ambulance); clearly marked placeholders for CityCare phone, address and ER hours; a 'Request a visit' form with name, phone, department and preferred date/time only; a short privacy notice beside the form; a demo banner stating it needs a real backend and consent handling; and a client-side confirmation saying the hospital will call to confirm, with no held appointment implied. The form makes no network calls and has no storage.
proposal.completion_check: Pass only if all hold: (1) the file opens from disk with no build step; (2) the form has exactly 4 fields and none for symptoms or history; (3) submit shows the 'hospital will call to confirm' message and the code has no fetch, XHR, form action, localStorage, sessionStorage, cookie or beacon calls; (4) the privacy notice and demo banner are visible; (5) 112 and 108 appear in the emergency section; (6) every CityCare phone, address and ER-hours value is visibly marked as a placeholder.
